facts.label: Analytical read-through
facts.text: - Usable coverage: an audited three-year annual set plus three consecutive unaudited quarters and three releases give a complete run of reporting dates from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026. The interim 10-Qs carry the December 31, 2025 balance sheet as comparative, which lets a downstream user tie the balance sheet to the audited annual report. - Strongest contrary evidence: the pack is filings only. The 10-Q states management's covenant position as "we were in compliance with the material covenants of our debt and lease agreements" (page:47) but prints no test level, so a reader cannot test headroom. The TrueBlue agreements are described as containing "debt service coverage ratios and minimum liquidity requirements" and "a cross-default to other material indebtedness" (page:47), and the notes and term loan are co-issued with a subsidiary partnership. A consumer that reads only the consolidated debt line would miss that this financing has its own tests and its own cross-default. - Source risk mechanism: debt, finance lease obligations and failed sale-leaseback obligations sit in one reported line ("Aircraft failed sale-leaseback transactions, due through 2036", Q3 10-Q page:11), and the debt note shows two totals on different bases. A consumer that picks a total without naming its basis, or that excludes the failed sale-leasebacks, would misstate fixed obligations. Operating lease liabilities, flight equipment purchase commitments and other obligations are reported outside the debt note (Q3 10-Q page:46 contractual obligations table), so they need separate handling downstream. - What cannot proceed: covenant headroom against agreement definitions, guarantor-level analysis, any rating-agency or market-implied view, and peer relative value from these sources. - Next evidence action: supply the TrueBlue indenture and term loan agreement and the Citibank credit agreement listed in the 10-K exhibit index, any covenant compliance certificates or levels, and any filings made between October 26, 2026 and 2026-11-05.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is usable. Audited FY2024 and FY2025 statements and unaudited statements for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 are located and tie to the earnings releases. Revenue grew in every 2026 quarter, but fuel and labor costs grew faster, so the operating result deteriorated year on year: the nine-month 2026 operating loss was 509 against 268 in the prior-year nine months. The issuer prints no EBITDA, so EBITDA here is operating income plus depreciation and amortization, with the separately printed special items added back; the unadjusted figure is shown beside it. On that basis leverage and interest cover are weak and worsen from FY2025 to the last twelve months, and the ratios are very sensitive to a small EBITDA denominator. Liquidity is 2,226 on a computed basis (cash, cash equivalents and investment securities plus the undrawn 600 Citibank revolver), which matches management's stated 2.2 billion. Maturities before 2029 are small relative to liquidity. Limits: the issuer reports no covenant levels, executed agreements are not supplied, and amounts are rounded to millions.

facts.label: Definition review and interpretation
facts.text: - EBITDA: no source prints the word EBITDA. EBITDA here is operating loss plus depreciation and amortization from the statements of operations, optionally plus the separately printed special items line. Aircraft rent (49 for nine months 2026) is not added back, so this is not EBITDAR. Capitalized interest is not adjusted. - Special items: Q3 2026 special items are a litigation reserve remeasurement; FY2024 special items of 591 include a non-cash Spirit item of 450 per the FY2025 10-K cash flow statement (page:114). Adding special items back is a choice that raises EBITDA; the unadjusted measure is shown. - Cash interest is "net" (net of interest income cash receipts per 10-K page:136), so it understates gross cash interest and the cover ratio is flattered by interest income. Interest income fell from 101 to 57 between the nine months of 2025 and 2026 (page:6). - Debt basis: the debt table totals 8,450 before issuance costs; the carrying value, fair value table and release use 8,393. Credit metrics here use carrying value so that they tie to the release and the balance sheet (current 482 plus non-current 7,911 equals 8,393). - Interpretation: fuel is the largest single driver of the deterioration. In Q3 2026 total operating expenses rose by 534 year on year, of which aircraft fuel accounts for 329 and salaries, wages and benefits for 81, against revenue growth of 490 (Q3 10-Q page:6). Operating cash flow was negative in both nine-month periods and free cash flow after capex and pre-delivery deposits was negative in every period shown, so capex and debt repayment in 2026 were met from the liquidity balance and from 495 of new secured borrowing: unrestricted cash and investments fell by 851 from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026 while 658 of debt and finance lease principal was repaid.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: JetBlue is a Delaware-incorporated, publicly listed US airline with one reportable segment, a point-to-point network centered on the Northeast corridor, six focus cities, and a loyalty program and co-brand card relationship that sit inside the TrueBlue secured financing. No sponsor, controlling holder or parent is identified in the supplied sources, and the context sponsor field is blank. There is no pending merger or acquisition: the merger agreement with Spirit Airlines was terminated on March 1, 2024, and the only 2026 acquisition is a set of 22 LaGuardia slots for a stated aggregate price, completed in October 2026 after the quarter end. The transaction relevant to creditors is financing, not ownership change: secured aircraft financing in April 2026 (fully drawn at September 30, 2026, with a further increment expected in the fourth quarter of 2026) and the earlier 2024 TrueBlue, equipment note and convertible issues. Operating risk is driven by fuel with no hedges, labor cost with open pilot and inflight negotiations, Northeast air traffic and weather disruption, and engine availability. Management language on a return to profitability in 2027 and an earnings target for 2028 is forward-looking and is recorded as Management Language, not as fact. Limits: ownership detail and the debt agreements are not supplied, and use of proceeds for the 2026 financing is not stated.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: No acquisition, merger, sponsor transaction or dividend recapitalisation is pending in the supplied sources. The historical transaction is the proposed combination with Spirit Airlines: the merger agreement was terminated by a termination agreement dated March 1, 2024, JetBlue paid a $69 million breakup fee on March 5, 2024, and prepayments to Spirit shareholders totalling $425 million were written off (10-K page:161, page:162). The related appeal over plaintiffs' attorneys' fees is stayed because of Spirit's bankruptcy filings (10-K page:162). In July 2026 JetBlue was selected as successful bidder for 22 operating authorizations at LaGuardia previously operated by Spirit for an aggregate purchase price of $58.5 million, and completed the acquisition in October 2026 after regulatory approval (Q3 10-Q page:44); this occurred after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet date and is a subsequent event, not part of Q3 2026 facts.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New debt in 2026: on April 14, 2026 JetBlue entered into an agreement for up to $500 million of debt financing secured by certain owned A321, A320 and A220 aircraft, fully borrowed by September 30, 2026, with maturities ranging from 2033 through 2036 and interest rates based on U.S. Treasury rates plus a margin; the agreement provides a further $250 million of incremental aircraft-secured financing, access requirements were satisfied during Q3 2026, and "Funding is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to the completion of customary funding mechanics" (Q3 10-Q page:13, page:14). On April 1, 2026 the 0.50% convertible senior notes were paid in full ($325 million of principal), partly from the Citibank escrow (Q3 10-Q page:13). The use of proceeds of the April 2026 financing is not stated in the sources, and the specific lender, security package and covenants of the agreement are not supplied (Insufficient Information). The August 2024 financings that remain outstanding are the TrueBlue senior secured notes (9.875% coupon, due September 2031, co-issued with JetBlue Loyalty, LP and guaranteed by the Guarantors), the TrueBlue term loan facility due 2029 and the 2.50% convertible senior notes due 2029 (10-K page:129, page:130, page:135). Liquidity effect and amounts outstanding are in CP-1; this handoff adds no new amounts.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: - Revenue durability. Evidence: demand "remained resilient across our network despite higher fares" (Q3 10-Q page:29) and revenue per available seat mile growth reported by management (Management Language). Mechanic: higher yields have offset fuel in part but volumes are flat to slightly higher and load factor fell year on year (Q3 release page:8), so durability depends on pricing power rather than volume. Implication: revenue is exposed to a demand downturn that cannot be offset by cost cuts quickly; CP-2 should treat the pricing recapture of fuel as unproven beyond the reported quarters. No logged conflict counters this. - Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: unhedged fuel, with a 10% fuel price rise equal to approximately $376 million of annual expense (Q3 10-Q page:53), and open labor contracts. Mechanic: operating margin and cash flow absorb fuel and wage shocks directly. Implication: CP-1 shows operating cash flow negative in FY2025 and in both nine-month periods and free cash flow negative in every period shown, so debt service and capital spending are met from liquidity and secured borrowing; monitoring posture is liquidity burn. - Concentration risk. Evidence: 95% of routes touch six focus cities and operations are centered in the Northeast corridor (10-K page:11, page:15). Mechanic: weather and air traffic control constraints affect a large share of capacity at once. Implication: disruption costs recur and can coincide with peak travel periods. - Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor or controlling holder identified; no dividends or repurchases. Mechanic: no sponsor extraction channel is documented. Implication: alignment risk is low on the evidence supplied, but beneficial ownership is Insufficient Information until the proxy statement is supplied. - Key uncertainties: the terms of the TrueBlue and aircraft financing covenants; the outcome of the antitrust class action and the American Airlines contract claim, for which no loss estimate is given for the former (Q3 10-Q page:21); labor outcomes; fuel path; and the funding of the further $250 million increment.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: JetBlue Airways Corporation is a weak but currently funded credit: operating earnings do not cover its debt service, so it is living on its balance sheet. The strongest support is USD 2,226 million of liquidity at September 30, 2026, which includes a USD 600 million undrawn revolver to October 2029, together with only USD 629 million of debt maturing through 2027 and continued access to aircraft-secured funding. The weakest point is earnings: computed last-twelve-months EBITDA excluding special items of USD 149 million covers cash interest of USD 493 million only 0.30x, and free cash flow was an outflow of USD 1,193 million. What decides the outcome is whether fares keep recapturing unhedged fuel cost through 2027, and whether unencumbered collateral remains available as cash falls.
facts.basis: Literal wrapped paragraph from the model-authored handoff; no new analysis.

citations.quote: JetBlue Airways Corporation is a weak but currently funded credit: operating earnings do not cover its debt service, so it is living on its balance sheet. The strongest support is USD 2,226 million of liquidity at September 30, 2026, which includes a USD 600 million undrawn revolver to October 2029, together with only USD 629 million of debt maturing through 2027 and continued access to aircraft-secured funding. The weakest point is earnings: computed last-twelve-months EBITDA excluding special items of USD 149 million covers cash interest of USD 493 million only 0.30x, and free cash flow was an outflow of USD 1,193 million. What decides the outcome is whether fares keep recapturing unhedged fuel cost through 2027, and whether unencumbered collateral remains available as cash falls.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, the earnings base is thin relative to the debt load. Computed EBITDA excluding special items was USD 350 million in FY2025 and USD 149 million for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, against debt of USD 8,393 million, which gives 56.33x gross and 45.42x net leverage [CP-1]. The issuer reports no EBITDA, so the ratios are our definition and are very sensitive to a small denominator; the direction is not in doubt, because the operating loss widened from USD 268 million to USD 509 million between the nine months of 2025 and 2026 [CP-1; Q3 10-Q page:6].

The issuer reports no EBITDA, so the ratios are our definition and are very sensitive to a small denominator; the direction is not in doubt, because the operating loss widened from USD 268 million to USD 509 million between the nine months of 2025 and 2026 [CP-1; Q3 10-Q page:6].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, the cash burn is funded by the liquidity cushion rather than by operations. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 273 million and free cash flow an outflow of USD 897 million in the nine months of 2026, while unrestricted cash and investments fell by USD 851 million to USD 1,626 million and net debt rose from USD 6,021 million to USD 6,767 million [CP-1]. The USD 495 million of new secured borrowing in 2026 offset only part of the USD 658 million of principal repaid.

citations.quote: Second, the cash burn is funded by the liquidity cushion rather than by operations. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 273 million and free cash flow an outflow of USD 897 million in the nine months of 2026, while unrestricted cash and investments fell by USD 851 million to USD 1,626 million and net debt rose from USD 6,021 million to USD 6,767 million [CP-1]. The USD 495 million of new secured borrowing in 2026 offset only part of the USD 658 million of principal repaid.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Third, the structure is predominantly secured. Secured instruments are USD 7,455 million of the USD 8,450 million gross debt and finance lease obligations, and unsecured instruments are USD 995 million (Q3 10-Q page:11; calculation below). Of the secured amount, USD 2,733 million is the TrueBlue notes and term loan, secured by a first lien on loyalty program collateral and co-issued with JetBlue Loyalty, LP (10-K page:129, page:130). The 10-Q states that "Approximately 66% of our owned property and equipment and intangible assets at net book value were pledged or committed to be pledged as security under various loan agreements" (Q3 10-Q page:47). Mechanic: each new secured borrowing moves unencumbered value to secured lenders ahead of the USD 995 million of unsecured claims and any future unsecured lender; management's claim of about USD 7 billion of unencumbered assets is attributed and not reconciled (Q3 release page:2).

citations.quote: Third, the structure is predominantly secured. Secured instruments are USD 7,455 million of the USD 8,450 million gross debt and finance lease obligations, and unsecured instruments are USD 995 million (Q3 10-Q page:11; calculation below). Of the secured amount, USD 2,733 million is the TrueBlue notes and term loan, secured by a first lien on loyalty program collateral and co-issued with JetBlue Loyalty, LP (10-K page:129, page:130). The 10-Q states that "Approximately 66% of our owned property and equipment and intangible assets at net book value were pledged or committed to be pledged as security under various loan agreements" (Q3 10-Q page:47). Mechanic: each new secured borrowing moves unencumbered value to secured lenders ahead of the USD 995 million of unsecured claims and any future unsecured lender; management's claim of about USD 7 billion of unencumbered assets is attributed and not reconciled (Q3 release page:2).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fourth, the maturity profile is back-ended. Debt maturing is USD 152 million for the remainder of 2026, USD 477 million in 2027, USD 582 million in 2028, USD 1,835 million in 2029, USD 656 million in 2030 and USD 4,691 million thereafter (Q3 10-Q page:11). The 2029 amount includes the maturity of the USD 460 million 2.50% convertible senior notes and of the TrueBlue term loan facility, and coincides with the October 21, 2029 revolver expiry. Liquidity covers the fixed claims through 2027 (see Calculations) provided the revolver remains available and its minimum liquidity covenant is met.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fifth, covenant headroom cannot be measured. Management states "we were in compliance with the material covenants of our debt and lease agreements" (Q3 10-Q page:47), but no level, step-down or reported ratio is printed for the TrueBlue financings or the Citibank revolver. The revolver "includes covenants that require us to maintain certain minimum balances in unrestricted cash, cash equivalents, and unused commitments available under revolving credit facilities" (10-K page:94). With unrestricted cash and investments falling, this is the test most likely to bind first; its level is Insufficient Information.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Sixth, operating exposures are unhedged and open-ended. The issuer had no fuel hedging contracts at September 30, 2026, and a 10% fuel price increase would add approximately USD 376 million of expense over twelve months (Q3 10-Q page:53). The pilot contract has been amendable since February 2025 and the inflight contract becomes amendable on December 13, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:19, page:20), so labor cost can step up without a revenue offset. Management says it recaptured approximately 87% of higher third-quarter fuel cost through fares (Q3 release page:1, Management Language); that recapture is the central assumption in any recovery of coverage.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Liquidity: USD 1,626 million of unrestricted cash, cash equivalents and investment securities plus the USD 600 million undrawn Citibank revolver gives USD 2,226 million, with no facility used in that figure expiring within twelve months [CP-1; Q3 10-Q page:14]. Documentary Fact. Funding access: the issuer borrowed USD 500 million against owned aircraft in 2026 and expects a further USD 250 million in the fourth quarter of 2026, which shows secured market access for aircraft collateral (Q3 10-Q page:13, page:14). Documentary Fact; the further amount is forward-looking. Governance: no sponsor or controlling holder is identified, no dividends are paid and no repurchase program exists [CP-1A; 10-K page:80], so no sponsor extraction channel is documented. Documentary Fact; beneficial ownership is Insufficient Information. Revenue momentum: Q3 2026 revenue of USD 2,812 million rose from USD 2,322 million in Q3 2025 [CP-1], with management attributing the growth to higher yields. Documentary Fact for the figures; Management Language for the attribution.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Earnings and coverage: the 0.30x cash interest cover and negative free cash flow above are the core weakness. Documentary Fact for the inputs; Analyst Interpretation for the credit reading. Rising net debt and a thinning equity base: stockholders' equity fell from USD 2,120 million to USD 1,337 million and retained earnings turned to a deficit of USD 106 million between December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:6). Documentary Fact. Encumbrance: about 88% of debt is secured and a large majority of fixed assets are pledged or committed to be pledged. Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation. Concentration and operating shocks: 95% of routes touch six focus cities in a congested Northeast corridor, and disruption plus engine groundings (two aircraft grounded at September 30, 2026) reduce completed capacity [CP-1A]. Documentary Fact. Contingencies: the Northeast Alliance antitrust class action cannot be estimated (Q3 10-Q page:21) and the American Airlines contract claim carries an accrual of unstated size (Q3 10-Q page:22). Documentary Fact; loss is Insufficient Information.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: - Secured gross debt at September 30, 2026: 43 + 409 + 128 + 38 + 407 + 73 + 573 + 619 + 2,011 + 1,991 + 742 + 421 = 7,455. Unsecured: 259 + 144 + 132 + 460 = 995. Total 7,455 + 995 = 8,450, equal to the gross total. Secured share 7,455 / 8,450 = 88.22 percent; unsecured share 11.78 percent (Q3 10-Q page:11). - TrueBlue: 1,991 + 742 = 2,733, which is 32.34 percent of 8,450. - Payroll support loans: 259 + 144 + 132 = 535. - Maturities through 2027: 152 + 477 = 629. Unrestricted cash and investments cover this 1,626 / 629 = 2.59x; total liquidity 2,226 / 629 = 3.54x. - Committed flight equipment spending for the remainder of 2026 and 2027: 185 + 385 = 570 (Q3 10-Q page:17). Maturities plus committed spending: 629 + 570 = 1,199. Liquidity 2,226 / 1,199 = 1.86x; unrestricted cash 1,626 / 1,199 = 1.36x. This is an illustrative comparison of fixed claims to liquidity before any operating cash flow, not a forecast. - Last-twelve-months free cash outflow 1,193 against unrestricted cash and investments 1,626: 1,193 / 1,626 = 73.37 percent [CP-1]. - Change in stockholders' equity: 1,337 - 2,120 = (783) (Q3 10-Q page:6). - Maturity shares of 8,393: 2029 1,835 / 8,393 = 21.86 percent; thereafter 4,691 / 8,393 = 55.89 percent; 2030 and thereafter (656 + 4,691) / 8,393 = 63.71 percent. - Interest sensitivity: fixed rate 6.3 billion plus floating rate 2.1 billion = 8.4 billion, consistent with 8,393; a 100 basis point rise would add approximately 21 of annual interest expense (Q3 10-Q page:53). FY2026 interest expense guidance of approximately 590 less nine months 2026 interest expense of 440 implies approximately 150 for Q4 2026 (Q3 release page:3; Q3 10-Q page:6), a derived figure from approximate guidance. - Net debt, from CP-1 inputs: December 31, 2025 8,498 - 2,477 = 6,021; September 30, 2026 8,393 - 1,626 = 6,767; increase 6,767 - 6,021 = 746. - Leverage, coverage, free cash flow and net debt figures are CP-1's and are not recomputed here; a recheck of the LTM ratios gives 8,393 / 149 = 56.33, 6,767 / 149 = 45.42 and 149 / 493 = 0.30.

## Findings
### Reader summary

### Readiness view

The view is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for all four requested consumers. The effective source set is one registrant's filed annual report, three filed quarterly reports and three furnished earnings releases, all dated before the as-of date, so each consumer can perform its own method; none is made CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. The limitations are that the pack contains no executed debt or lease agreements, no investor presentations, no ratings or market data, and only text extractions in which tables are flattened. These bounds carry into each consumer's assessment below. Source sufficiency is not completion of any downstream analysis.
| Consumer | Status | Basis | Command sheet |

| CP-1 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Audited FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023 statements and unaudited statements for each of Q1 2026, Q2 2026 and Q3 2026 with comparatives are located. Limits: text extraction flattens tables; no XBRL or original layout is supplied. | RUN |

| CP-1A | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business description, strategy, fleet, labor, Blue Sky and TrueBlue financing narrative, litigation and later events are located in the 10-K and 10-Qs. Limits: the exhibit-listed agreements and any proxy statement are not supplied. | RUN |

| CP-5 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | All seven sources carry stable chunk numbers, so claims can be traced. Limits: visual and table-layout checks against the filed HTML are not possible from text. | RUN |
### Source register

- Family and authority: filed annual report; original authority for audited FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023 results. Cover, page:1: "For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025". Registrant, page:1: "JETBLUE AIRWAYS CORPORATION (Exact name of registrant as specified in its charter)".

- Audit: page:108 "We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of JetBlue Airways Corporation (the Company) as of December 31, 2025 and 2024". Auditor tenure, page:109: "We have served as the Company’s auditor since 2001." Report date, page:109: "New York, New York February 12, 2026". The internal-control opinion is unqualified (page:108: "expressed an unqualified opinion thereon").

- Statements located: balance sheets page:112 ("TOTAL ASSETS $ 16,570 $ 16,841" is the December 31, 2025 and 2024 pair on the asset side), statements of operations page:113, cash flows page:114. Units, page:113: "(in millions, except per share data)". USD.
- Perimeter: one consolidated registrant; page:159 "JetBlue has one reportable operating segment, air transportation services."
- Debt: financing narrative at page:129 and page:130 (TrueBlue notes and term loan); market-risk and covenant description at page:94 and page:97.
- Exhibit index at page:168 onwards lists indentures and credit agreements by title; the agreements themselves are not supplied.
#### Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 (10-Q_2026-03-31_jblu-20260331.htm.jsonl)
- Family and authority: filed, unaudited quarterly report. Page:1: "For the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026". Signature, page:47: "Date: April 28, 2026".

- Statements: operations page:6 with "Three Months Ended March 31,"; basis is quarter only (no year-to-date column for Q1). Liquidity statement located on page:30: "At March 31, 2026, we had $2.4 billion in liquidity".
- Version relationship: the Q1 report remains a separate active source and is not collapsed into the later reports.
#### Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (10-Q_2026-06-30_jblu-20260630.htm.jsonl)
- Family and authority: filed, unaudited. Page:1: "For the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026". Signature, page:54: "Date: July 28, 2026".
- Statements: operations page:6 with "Three Months Ended June 30, Six Months Ended June 30," so quarter and six-month year-to-date are both labelled.
#### Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl)
- Family and authority: filed, unaudited; the latest filed financial report in the pack. Page:1: "For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2026". Signature, page:54: "Date: October 26, 2026".

- Statements: balance sheets page:5 and page:6 ("September 30, 2026 December 31, 2025"), operations page:6 ("Three Months Ended September 30, Nine Months Ended September 30,"), cash flows page:7 ("Nine Months Ended September 30,"), units page:5 "(in millions, except per share data)". USD.

- Debt: Note 3 at page:11 to page:15 holds the instrument table, the maturity table, fair value and the Citibank and Morgan Stanley lines. Liquidity at page:44, covenant statement at page:47, commitments at page:17, market risk at page:53.

- Perimeter note: the debt note describes TrueBlue notes "co-issued with JetBlue Loyalty LP" (page:47: "In August 2024, JetBlue co-issued with JetBlue Loyalty LP"). The statements are consolidated; no stand-alone statements for JetBlue Loyalty LP are supplied.

- Basis note: two debt totals appear with different bases. Page:11: "Total debt and finance lease obligations $ 8,450 $ 8,560" before issuance costs, and page:12: "Total Debt $ 8,393 $ 7,620 $ 8,498 $ 7,829" as carrying value net of issuance costs followed by fair value. A downstream user must name which basis is used.
#### Earnings releases, Exhibit 99.1 (three files)

- Family and authority: issuer press releases furnished with Form 8-K; management-prepared and unaudited, so they give attributed supporting claims and do not override the filings. Q1 page:2 "JETBLUE ANNOUNCES FIRST QUARTER 2026 RESULTS"; Q2 page:1 "JETBLUE ANNOUNCES SECOND QUARTER 2026 RESULTS" and "NEW YORK (July 28, 2026)"; Q3 page:1 "JETBLUE ANNOUNCES THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS" and "NEW YORK (October 26, 2026)".

- Content: statements of operations, operating statistics, selected balance sheet and cash-flow data, and non-GAAP reconciliations (Q3 page:9 "Note A - Non-GAAP Financial Measures"; page:11 reconciliation excluding special items and gain on investments). Guidance basis, Q3 page:4: "Revised guidance as of September 10, 2026."

- Version relationship: the release statements of operations repeat the 10-Q statements (Q3 page:7 and the 10-Q page:6 both show "Total operating revenues 2,812 2,322 7,749 6,818"). Treat the 10-Q as controlling for statement facts and the release as supporting, not independent, corroboration.
- Management claims to be attributed, not verified from filings: Q3 page:2 "Expanded unencumbered asset base to ~$7 billion".
- Non-GAAP: CASM ex-fuel, adjusted operating margin and loss per share excluding special items are management measures, not GAAP.
### Information-availability boundary

- Latest dated evidence: the Q3 10-Q and Q3 release, both dated October 26, 2026, which is before the as-of date and cutoff 2026-11-05. No source is dated after the cutoff. Text of future dates in the sources, for example the inflight crewmember contract "amendable date of December 13, 2026" (Q3 10-Q page:19) and a BlueFirst service start in December 2026, is forward-looking and labelled as such there.
- Events between October 26, 2026 and 2026-11-05 are Not supplied, not absent.

- Subsequent events inside the filings: Q3 10-Q page:44 "Following receipt of regulatory approval, the Company completed the acquisition in October 2026" (22 LaGuardia slots previously operated by Spirit Airlines); page:14 additional aircraft-secured financing "Funding is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026"; page:21 "On October 9, 2026, the Company and American filed a brief opposing that class certification".
### Identity and perimeter
- Reporting entity: JetBlue Airways Corporation, Delaware (10-K page:1), a single consolidated registrant with one reportable segment (10-K page:159).

- Issuer, borrower and guarantor roles: the filings name JetBlue and JetBlue Loyalty LP as co-issuers of the TrueBlue notes (10-K page:129: "co-issued $2.0 billion aggregate principal amount of senior secured notes due 2031"). Guarantor identities are in the indenture, which is not supplied. Equipment notes and EETCs are issued by the Company, with pass-through trusts that are not consolidated (Q3 10-Q page:13: "we have not consolidated these trusts in our financial statements").
- Unresolved: no restricted-group, parent or stand-alone Loyalty LP statements; the context leaves these fields blank.
### Consumer evidence demand
| Consumer | Evidence it needs | Located | Limitation carried forward |

| CP-1 | Annual and interim statements, debt, liquidity, cash flows, non-GAAP | 10-K page:112 to page:114; 10-Q Q3 page:5 to page:7, page:11 to page:15; releases | Text extraction; two debt bases; quarter versus year-to-date labels must be kept; non-GAAP is management-defined |

| CP-1A | Business, fleet, strategy, labor, ownership of financings, later events | 10-K page:9; Q3 10-Q page:31 to page:33, page:19 | No agreements or proxy statement; no stand-alone Loyalty LP view |

| CP-2 | CP-1 and CP-1A outputs, maturity wall, liquidity, covenants, commitments | Q3 10-Q page:12, page:17, page:44, page:46 to page:47 | Covenant levels and headroom not printed; pledged assets stated only as share and net book value |
| CP-5 | Traceable claims | All seven sources carry chunk numbers | No original layout or XBRL; chunk numbers differ from printed pages |
### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: an audited three-year annual set plus three consecutive unaudited quarters and three releases give a complete run of reporting dates from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026. The interim 10-Qs carry the December 31, 2025 balance sheet as comparative, which lets a downstream user tie the balance sheet to the audited annual report.

- Strongest contrary evidence: the pack is filings only. The 10-Q states management's covenant position as "we were in compliance with the material covenants of our debt and lease agreements" (page:47) but prints no test level, so a reader cannot test headroom. The TrueBlue agreements are described as containing "debt service coverage ratios and minimum liquidity requirements" and "a cross-default to other material indebtedness" (page:47), and the notes and term loan are co-issued with a subsidiary partnership. A consumer that reads only the consolidated debt line would miss that this financing has its own tests and its own cross-default.

- Source risk mechanism: debt, finance lease obligations and failed sale-leaseback obligations sit in one reported line ("Aircraft failed sale-leaseback transactions, due through 2036", Q3 10-Q page:11), and the debt note shows two totals on different bases. A consumer that picks a total without naming its basis, or that excludes the failed sale-leasebacks, would misstate fixed obligations. Operating lease liabilities, flight equipment purchase commitments and other obligations are reported outside the debt note (Q3 10-Q page:46 contractual obligations table), so they need separate handling downstream.
- What cannot proceed: covenant headroom against agreement definitions, guarantor-level analysis, any rating-agency or market-implied view, and peer relative value from these sources.

- Next evidence action: supply the TrueBlue indenture and term loan agreement and the Citibank credit agreement listed in the 10-K exhibit index, any covenant compliance certificates or levels, and any filings made between October 26, 2026 and 2026-11-05.

No new calculation. CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Figures quoted above are reproduced from the cited locators only.

| Text extraction only: tables are flattened and no XBRL or original layout is supplied | Medium | CP-1, CP-5 | Check figures against the filed HTML when a number drives a conclusion |
| Two debt totals on different bases (gross of issuance costs versus carrying value) | Low | CP-1, CP-2 | Name the basis in every downstream use |
| Events after October 26, 2026 up to 2026-11-05 are not supplied | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply later 8-K filings or confirm none |

| Revised guidance dated September 10, 2026 is referenced in the Q3 release but the announcement itself is not supplied | Low | CP-1A | Supply the September 10, 2026 announcement if guidance changes matter |

### Financial base view

The financial base is usable. Audited FY2024 and FY2025 statements and unaudited statements for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 are located and tie to the earnings releases. Revenue grew in every 2026 quarter, but fuel and labor costs grew faster, so the operating result deteriorated year on year: the nine-month 2026 operating loss was 509 against 268 in the prior-year nine months. The issuer prints no EBITDA, so EBITDA here is operating income plus depreciation and amortization, with the separately printed special items added back; the unadjusted figure is shown beside it. On that basis leverage and interest cover are weak and worsen from FY2025 to the last twelve months, and the ratios are very sensitive to a small EBITDA denominator. Liquidity is 2,226 on a computed basis (cash, cash equivalents and investment securities plus the undrawn 600 Citibank revolver), which matches management's stated 2.2 billion. Maturities before 2029 are small relative to liquidity. Limits: the issuer reports no covenant levels, executed agreements are not supplied, and amounts are rounded to millions.

### Liquidity, covenants and ratings

- Liquidity at September 30, 2026: management states "$2.2 billion in liquidity, which includes $1.6 billion in unrestricted cash, cash equivalents, and investment securities and our $600 million undrawn Citibank line of credit" (Q3 10-Q page:44). Our computed total of 2,226 agrees. Management expects liquidity to be sufficient for at least the next 12 months (page:44).

- Facility expiry: the Citibank revolver of 600 matures October 21, 2029 (Q3 10-Q page:14); no facility used in liquidity expires within twelve months of the as-of date. The Morgan Stanley line is not committed to a fixed amount.

- Covenants: the Citibank revolver includes covenants requiring minimum balances of unrestricted cash, cash equivalents and unused commitments (10-K page:94). The TrueBlue notes and term loan carry "debt service coverage ratios and minimum liquidity requirements" and a cross-default to other material indebtedness (Q3 10-Q page:47). Management states "we were in compliance with the material covenants of our debt and lease agreements" (Q3 10-Q page:47). No level, step-down or reported ratio is printed, so headroom is Not calculable.

- Security: the net book value of pledged assets is $8.0 billion (Q3 10-Q page:11) and approximately 66% of owned property and equipment and intangibles are pledged or committed to be pledged (page:47). Management claims an unencumbered asset base of about $7 billion (Q3 release page:2); this is attributed to management and is not reconciled to the filing.
- Ratings: none supplied (context ratings field is blank).

- Q3 2026 against Q3 2025: total operating revenues 2,812 against 2,322; aircraft fuel 868 against 539; operating loss (144) against (100); net loss (257) against (143) (Q3 10-Q page:6). Management reports average fuel price per gallon of $3.91 against $2.49 (Q3 release page:8).

- Financing events in 2026: 0.50% convertible senior notes of 325 repaid April 1, 2026, partly from the 100 Citibank escrow (page:14); aircraft-secured financing of up to $500 million agreed April 14, 2026 and fully borrowed by September 30, 2026, maturities 2033 through 2036; a further $250 million is available and "Funding is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026" (page:14).

- Subsequent events up to the cutoff: acquisition of 22 LaGuardia slots from Spirit Airlines completed in October 2026 for an aggregate purchase price of $58.5 million (page:44); opposition to class certification filed October 9, 2026 (page:21). Nothing after October 26, 2026 is supplied.
- Other: supplemental agreements with IAE dated July 27, 2026 give credits up to $105 million against future purchases through December 31, 2027 (page:33).
### Definition review and interpretation

- EBITDA: no source prints the word EBITDA. EBITDA here is operating loss plus depreciation and amortization from the statements of operations, optionally plus the separately printed special items line. Aircraft rent (49 for nine months 2026) is not added back, so this is not EBITDAR. Capitalized interest is not adjusted.

- Special items: Q3 2026 special items are a litigation reserve remeasurement; FY2024 special items of 591 include a non-cash Spirit item of 450 per the FY2025 10-K cash flow statement (page:114). Adding special items back is a choice that raises EBITDA; the unadjusted measure is shown.

- Cash interest is "net" (net of interest income cash receipts per 10-K page:136), so it understates gross cash interest and the cover ratio is flattered by interest income. Interest income fell from 101 to 57 between the nine months of 2025 and 2026 (page:6).

- Debt basis: the debt table totals 8,450 before issuance costs; the carrying value, fair value table and release use 8,393. Credit metrics here use carrying value so that they tie to the release and the balance sheet (current 482 plus non-current 7,911 equals 8,393).

- Interpretation: fuel is the largest single driver of the deterioration. In Q3 2026 total operating expenses rose by 534 year on year, of which aircraft fuel accounts for 329 and salaries, wages and benefits for 81, against revenue growth of 490 (Q3 10-Q page:6). Operating cash flow was negative in both nine-month periods and free cash flow after capex and pre-delivery deposits was negative in every period shown, so capex and debt repayment in 2026 were met from the liquidity balance and from 495 of new secured borrowing: unrestricted cash and investments fell by 851 from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026 while 658 of debt and finance lease principal was repaid.

Gross cash flow explains an increase of 495 raised less 658 repaid, plus 44 of flight equipment acquired under finance leases (Q3 10-Q page:7): 8,560 + 495 - 658 + 44 = 8,441 against the reported 8,450 before issuance costs; the residual of 9 is not itemized in the sources.
### EBITDA
- Computed EBITDA = operating income (loss) + depreciation and amortization.

### Net debt and liquidity

- Unrestricted cash, equivalents and investment securities. December 31, 2024: 1,921 + 1,689 + 336 = 3,946. December 31, 2025: 1,946 + 213 + 318 = 2,477. September 30, 2026: 1,258 + 251 + 117 = 1,626.

- Issuer: JETBLUE AIRWAYS CORP (registrant "JETBLUE AIRWAYS CORPORATION", ticker JBLU). As-of date 2026-11-05; information cutoff 2026-11-05.
- Pathway `credit_snapshot`, reporting currency USD, current period Q3 2026, prior period FY2025 (context). Amounts are US$ millions unless stated.

- Reader question: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to the creditor, with the chain evidence, risk mechanic, credit implication. Decision drivers: transaction and ownership structure; business and operating model; credit-relevant history or change.

- Scope limits: no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation, no recovery conclusion. Sector and country labels come from the run context, which is not issuer evidence; every other fact is cited to a pinned filing. Fact categories used: Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation, Insufficient Information.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| JetBlue is a point-to-point East Coast airline with no sponsor or controlling holder identified and no pending merger; the credit story is fuel-exposed operations funded by asset-backed debt, with the TrueBlue loyalty financing the key structural feature. | Medium | Ownership detail sits in an unsupplied proxy statement and debt agreements are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| No controlling holder or sponsor is identified; the Spirit merger was terminated in March 2024 and no acquisition is pending. | No sponsor extraction or deal-funding risk is evident, but ownership detail is incomplete. | Medium |

| Costs are concentrated in fuel and labor; fuel is unhedged and the pilot contract has been amendable since February 2025. | Fuel and wage shocks hit margins directly and cash conversion depends on liquidity. | High |

| The loyalty program is pledged as first-lien collateral for the TrueBlue notes and term loan. | A key cash-generating asset is committed to secured lenders, which matters for unsecured claims. | Medium |

| New 2026 secured financing is aircraft-backed, with a further increment expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. | Asset-backed funding continues, while use of proceeds is not stated in detail. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

JetBlue is a Delaware-incorporated, publicly listed US airline with one reportable segment, a point-to-point network centered on the Northeast corridor, six focus cities, and a loyalty program and co-brand card relationship that sit inside the TrueBlue secured financing. No sponsor, controlling holder or parent is identified in the supplied sources, and the context sponsor field is blank. There is no pending merger or acquisition: the merger agreement with Spirit Airlines was terminated on March 1, 2024, and the only 2026 acquisition is a set of 22 LaGuardia slots for a stated aggregate price, completed in October 2026 after the quarter end. The transaction relevant to creditors is financing, not ownership change: secured aircraft financing in April 2026 (fully drawn at September 30, 2026, with a further increment expected in the fourth quarter of 2026) and the earlier 2024 TrueBlue, equipment note and convertible issues. Operating risk is driven by fuel with no hedges, labor cost with open pilot and inflight negotiations, Northeast air traffic and weather disruption, and engine availability. Management language on a return to profitability in 2027 and an earnings target for 2028 is forward-looking and is recorded as Management Language, not as fact. Limits: ownership detail and the debt agreements are not supplied, and use of proceeds for the 2026 financing is not stated.
### Company and operating model
| Area | Fact or measure | Category | Locator | Risk mechanic and credit implication |

| Business | Scheduled passenger airline serving 112 destinations as of December 31, 2025 ("New York's Hometown Airline") | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:9 | Single reportable segment (10-K page:159) means no diversification across businesses; all credit capacity rests on air transportation cash flow. |

| Network | Predominantly point-to-point; 95% of routes touch at least one of six focus cities: New York metropolitan area, Boston, Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood, Orlando, Los Angeles and San Juan | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:11 | Concentration in congested Northeast airspace exposes completion and cost to weather and air traffic control constraints (Q3 10-Q page:31 describes Q3 2026 disruption). |

| Geography by capacity (FY2025 share of available seat miles) | Transcontinental 26.0%; Caribbean and Latin America 36.5%; Florida 25.4%; other (East, Central, West) 7.0%; Transatlantic 5.1% | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:12 | Leisure and VFR weighting gives seasonality; 10-K notes leisure carriers face high seasonality (page:12). |

| Revenue model | Passenger and other revenue; fares in core, EvenMore and Mint cabins; ancillary through the website, global distribution systems and Paisly vacation packages; domestic first class (BlueFirst) planned | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:10, page:11; Q3 10-Q page:6 | Premium and loyalty initiatives aim to lift yield; they are unproven and partly capex-funded, so near-term cash conversion is not helped. |

| Loyalty and co-brand | TrueBlue program; co-branded cards in the United States issued with Barclaycard on the Mastercard network; loyalty points liability at September 30, 2026 of 1,342 | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:14, page:15; Q3 10-Q page:10 | Loyalty cash and collateral support the TrueBlue notes and term loan; the same asset cannot also support unsecured claims. |

| Partnerships | Blue Sky collaboration with United Airlines announced May 2025; cross-merchandising from February 2026; more than 1.1 billion TrueBlue points redeemed on United flights | Documentary Fact (Management Language for the benefits) | 10-K page:13; Q3 10-Q page:31 | Revenue benefit is management-stated and unquantified in the sources; treat as upside not base case. |

| Fuel | No outstanding fuel hedging contracts at September 30, 2026; a hypothetical 10% fuel price increase would raise aircraft fuel expense by approximately $376 million over the next 12 months | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:53 | Unhedged fuel passes oil moves straight to operating margin; recovery depends on fare actions (management says it recaptured approximately 87% of higher Q3 fuel cost, Q3 release page:1, Management Language). |

| Labor | 49% of active full-time-equivalent crewmembers are union represented; pilots 21% and inflight 28%; pilot contract amendable since February 2025 with negotiations ongoing; inflight contract amendable December 13, 2026; TWU won dispatcher election, negotiations begin December 2026 | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:19, page:20 | Open contracts are a cost-escalation risk and a strike or slowdown risk (listed in the risk factors) bearing on margin and cash conversion. |

| Fleet | Operating fleet of 298 aircraft at September 30, 2026 (A220 67, A320 129, A321 63, A321neo 39): 288 owned and 10 leased; average age 12 years; 2 further aircraft held for sale | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:47 | Owned fleet supports secured borrowing (pledged net book value $8.0 billion, Q3 10-Q page:11) but leaves refinancing exposed to aircraft values. |

| Capital spending | Committed flight equipment expenditures of 5,372 including 77 aircraft deliveries; management expects annual capital expenditures below $1 billion through the end of the decade | Documentary Fact (Management Language for the expectation) | Q3 10-Q page:17, page:33 | Large fixed commitments reduce flexibility; deferral of deliveries has been used to protect cash (Q3 10-Q page:43). |

| Engine availability | Two aircraft grounded for lack of engine availability at September 30, 2026; management expects groundings to stay in single digits through 2026; IAE supplemental agreements of July 27, 2026 give credits of up to $105 million through December 31, 2027 | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:33 | Capacity loss and shop-visit delay hit revenue; the credits are vendor consideration, not cash. |

| Working capital | Working capital deficit of $1.6 billion at September 30, 2026, driven by air traffic liability; air traffic liability current 1,925 and non-current 771 | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:46, page:6 | Customer prepayments fund operations; a demand shock or processor holdback would drain cash quickly. |

| Credit card processors | Agreements contain no covenants but allow processors to withhold cash reserves; no collateral requirement at present | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:18 | A holdback right is a liquidity trigger in stress; not currently invoked per the filing. |
### Company profile
| Item | Value | Category | Locator |
| Legal entity | JetBlue Airways Corporation, Delaware, incorporated August 1998, service from February 11, 2000 | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:1, page:9 |
| Sector and country | Air Transportation, Scheduled; United States | Documentary Fact from the run context (not issuer evidence) | context |
| Listing | Common stock, NASDAQ, symbol JBLU | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:1 |
| Headquarters | 27-01 Queens Plaza North, Long Island City, New York | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:1 |
| Shares outstanding | 377,351,854 at September 30, 2026 (370,119,668 at January 31, 2026) | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:1; 10-K page:2 |
| Holders of record | Approximately 350 as of January 31, 2026 | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:80 |
| Employees | Approximately 23,000 crewmembers (10-K); average 19,882 full-time equivalents in Q3 2026 | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:9; Q3 release page:8 |

| Ownership | No sponsor, controlling holder or parent identified in the supplied sources; principal holders are in the 2026 proxy statement, which is not supplied | Insufficient Information | 10-K page:166 (Item 12 incorporates the proxy statement by reference) |
| Dividends and buybacks | "We have not paid cash dividends on our common stock and have no current intention to do so"; no share repurchase program | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:80 |

| Auditor | Ernst & Young LLP, auditor since 2001; opinion that the FY2025 statements present fairly, in all material respects, and an unqualified opinion on internal control | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:108, page:109 |
| Strategy framework | JetForward, announced July 2024: reliable service, East Coast leisure network, products and perks, secure financial future | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:9 |

| Management targets | Return to sustained operating profitability in 2027; at least $1.00 earnings per share and positive free cash flow in 2028 | Management Language | Q3 release page:1; Q2 release page:1 |

| Guidance | FY2026 adjusted operating margin of (4.5%) to (6.5%), interest expense approximately $590 million, capital expenditures approximately $850 million | Management Language | Q3 release page:3 |
| Equity-linked instruments | Warrants issued to the U.S. Treasury under payroll support programs; 2.50% convertible senior notes due 2029 | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:131, page:135 |
### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No acquisition, merger, sponsor transaction or dividend recapitalisation is pending in the supplied sources. The historical transaction is the proposed combination with Spirit Airlines: the merger agreement was terminated by a termination agreement dated March 1, 2024, JetBlue paid a $69 million breakup fee on March 5, 2024, and prepayments to Spirit shareholders totalling $425 million were written off (10-K page:161, page:162). The related appeal over plaintiffs' attorneys' fees is stayed because of Spirit's bankruptcy filings (10-K page:162). In July 2026 JetBlue was selected as successful bidder for 22 operating authorizations at LaGuardia previously operated by Spirit for an aggregate purchase price of $58.5 million, and completed the acquisition in October 2026 after regulatory approval (Q3 10-Q page:44); this occurred after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet date and is a subsequent event, not part of Q3 2026 facts.

New debt in 2026: on April 14, 2026 JetBlue entered into an agreement for up to $500 million of debt financing secured by certain owned A321, A320 and A220 aircraft, fully borrowed by September 30, 2026, with maturities ranging from 2033 through 2036 and interest rates based on U.S. Treasury rates plus a margin; the agreement provides a further $250 million of incremental aircraft-secured financing, access requirements were satisfied during Q3 2026, and "Funding is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to the completion of customary funding mechanics" (Q3 10-Q page:13, page:14). On April 1, 2026 the 0.50% convertible senior notes were paid in full ($325 million of principal), partly from the Citibank escrow (Q3 10-Q page:13). The use of proceeds of the April 2026 financing is not stated in the sources, and the specific lender, security package and covenants of the agreement are not supplied (Insufficient Information). The August 2024 financings that remain outstanding are the TrueBlue senior secured notes (9.875% coupon, due September 2031, co-issued with JetBlue Loyalty, LP and guaranteed by the Guarantors), the TrueBlue term loan facility due 2029 and the 2.50% convertible senior notes due 2029 (10-K page:129, page:130, page:135). Liquidity effect and amounts outstanding are in CP-1; this handoff adds no new amounts.
### Timeline
| Date | Event | Category | Locator |
| August 1998; February 11, 2000 | Incorporated in Delaware; commenced service | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:9 |

| July 2020; August 18, 2023 | Northeast Alliance with American Airlines formed; permanently enjoined effective August 18, 2023; wind-down substantially complete | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:21 |
| March 1, 2024; March 5, 2024 | Spirit merger agreement terminated; $69 million breakup fee paid | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:161 |
| July 2024 | JetForward framework announced | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:9 |
| August 2024 | TrueBlue notes and term loan; 2.50% convertible senior notes | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:129, page:130, page:135 |
| February 28, 2025 | First Amendment to TrueBlue term loan sets margin of SOFR plus 4.75% | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:130 |
| April 28, 2025 | American Airlines sued JetBlue in Texas over a Northeast Alliance revenue-sharing agreement; an accrual has been recorded | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:22 |
| May 2025 | Blue Sky collaboration with United Airlines announced | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:13 |
| October 27, 2025 | Citibank escrow agreement to keep the revolver expiry at October 21, 2029; $100 million funded before December 31, 2025 | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:137 |
| April 1, 2026 | 0.50% convertible senior notes paid in full | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:13 |
| April 14, 2026 | Agreement for up to $500 million of aircraft-secured financing | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:13 |
| July 27, 2026 | Supplemental support agreements with IAE (RTX) | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:33 |
| July 2026 (completed October 2026) | LaGuardia slots acquisition, aggregate purchase price $58.5 million | Documentary Fact; completion is a Subsequent event | Q3 10-Q page:44 |
| October 9, 2026 | Opposition to class certification filed in the Northeast Alliance antitrust matter | Documentary Fact; Subsequent event | Q3 10-Q page:21 |
| Fourth quarter of 2026 | Expected funding of the additional $250 million secured financing | Management Language (forward-looking) | Q3 10-Q page:14 |

| December 2026 | BlueFirst initial service planned; inflight contract amendable December 13, 2026 | Management Language (forward-looking); Documentary Fact for the contract date | Q3 release page:3; Q3 10-Q page:19 |
### Governance and behaviour
- Scope: issuer-level behaviour from documented actions only; no individuals assessed and no inference from identity.

- Distributions: no cash dividends and no repurchase program (10-K page:80); the cash flow statement shows one small treasury stock acquisition line of unstated purpose (Q3 10-Q page:7, nine months 2026). Category: Neutral or Mixed; no distribution to shareholders is documented. Dimension: payout behaviour.

- Use of secured capacity: the loyalty program is first-lien collateral for the TrueBlue notes and term loan, with a co-borrower subsidiary and Guarantors (10-K page:129, page:130); aircraft-secured borrowing continued in 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:13). Category: Neutral or Mixed. Mechanic: secured funding of operating losses converts unencumbered assets into secured claims over time, so unsecured creditors rank behind a larger secured pool; 66% of owned property and equipment and intangibles were pledged or committed to be pledged (Q3 10-Q page:47). This is an observation of structure, not evidence of priming or collateral release, and no non-pro-rata exchange, drop-down or uptier is documented.

- Disclosure: audited and unqualified opinions (10-K page:108); quarterly reports with covenant compliance statement (Q3 10-Q page:47). Category: Supportive on timeliness; Insufficient Information on covenant levels.

- Shareholder pressure: the 10-K states the Company "has been and may continue to be subject to actions from activist shareholders" (10-K page:44). Category: Documentary Fact; no specific activist or demand is identified in the sources, so no behaviour conclusion is drawn.

- Legal capacity versus willingness versus feasibility: legal capacity cannot be assessed because the debt agreements are not supplied; documented willingness is no distributions and continued secured borrowing; feasibility is shown by liquidity and market access in CP-1, which reports declining unrestricted cash and investments, so feasibility of further large debt-funded actions is limited by collateral availability. Evidence quality: High for filings, Low for management outlook statements.
### Conflicts and unreconciled items
- No document conflict is logged between the supplied sources on transaction size, ownership or dates.

- Unreconciled, not a conflict: management claims an unencumbered asset base of approximately $7 billion (Q3 release page:2) while the 10-Q states approximately 66% of owned property and equipment and intangibles are pledged or committed to be pledged (Q3 10-Q page:47) and $8.0 billion net book value is pledged (Q3 10-Q page:11). The definitions differ and the sources do not reconcile them; CP-2 should not rely on the management figure.
- Different bases, not a conflict: the debt note total before issuance costs differs from the carrying value (see CP-0 and CP-1).
### Credit translations

- Revenue durability. Evidence: demand "remained resilient across our network despite higher fares" (Q3 10-Q page:29) and revenue per available seat mile growth reported by management (Management Language). Mechanic: higher yields have offset fuel in part but volumes are flat to slightly higher and load factor fell year on year (Q3 release page:8), so durability depends on pricing power rather than volume. Implication: revenue is exposed to a demand downturn that cannot be offset by cost cuts quickly; CP-2 should treat the pricing recapture of fuel as unproven beyond the reported quarters. No logged conflict counters this.

- Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: unhedged fuel, with a 10% fuel price rise equal to approximately $376 million of annual expense (Q3 10-Q page:53), and open labor contracts. Mechanic: operating margin and cash flow absorb fuel and wage shocks directly. Implication: CP-1 shows operating cash flow negative in FY2025 and in both nine-month periods and free cash flow negative in every period shown, so debt service and capital spending are met from liquidity and secured borrowing; monitoring posture is liquidity burn.

- Concentration risk. Evidence: 95% of routes touch six focus cities and operations are centered in the Northeast corridor (10-K page:11, page:15). Mechanic: weather and air traffic control constraints affect a large share of capacity at once. Implication: disruption costs recur and can coincide with peak travel periods.

- Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor or controlling holder identified; no dividends or repurchases. Mechanic: no sponsor extraction channel is documented. Implication: alignment risk is low on the evidence supplied, but beneficial ownership is Insufficient Information until the proxy statement is supplied.

- Key uncertainties: the terms of the TrueBlue and aircraft financing covenants; the outcome of the antitrust class action and the American Airlines contract claim, for which no loss estimate is given for the former (Q3 10-Q page:21); labor outcomes; fuel path; and the funding of the further $250 million increment.
### Consumers
| Module | Readiness | What it should take from this handoff | Why it matters | Gap and required action |

| CP-2 | Ready with limitations | Collateral structure (loyalty program and aircraft), absence of sponsor, labor and fuel exposure, financing timeline | Defines the secured versus unsecured claim structure and the risks to margin | Supply the TrueBlue indenture, term loan and aircraft financing documents; do not use the unreconciled unencumbered asset claim |

| CP-5 | Ready with limitations | Fact categories, locators and the unreconciled items list | Traceability of management language versus filed fact | Spot-check quoted figures against the filed HTML |
## Calculations
All inputs are cited above. No figure from CP-1 is changed.
- Passenger revenue share, nine months 2026: 7,135 / 7,749 = 92.08 percent. Q3 2026: 2,600 / 2,812 = 92.46 percent (Q3 10-Q page:6).

- Fuel share of total operating expenses: Q3 2026 868 / 2,956 = 29.36 percent; nine months 2026 2,352 / 8,258 = 28.48 percent. Salaries, wages and benefits share: Q3 2026 946 / 2,956 = 32.00 percent; nine months 2026 2,717 / 8,258 = 32.90 percent (Q3 10-Q page:6).
- Fleet: 67 + 129 + 63 + 39 = 298 operating aircraft, equal to 288 owned + 10 leased (Q3 10-Q page:47).
- Union representation: 21 + 28 = 49 percent (Q3 10-Q page:19).
- Capacity distribution FY2025: 26.0 + 36.5 + 25.4 + 7.0 + 5.1 = 100.0 percent (10-K page:12).
- Committed deliveries: 33 A220 + 44 A321neo = 77 (Q3 10-Q page:17).
- Share count change from January 31, 2026 to September 30, 2026: 377,351,854 - 370,119,668 = 7,232,186 shares, 1.95 percent of the January figure.
- LaGuardia slots: $58.5 million / 22 = $2.66 million per authorization (an average derived for context only).

- Spirit termination costs: $69 million breakup fee and $425 million total prepayments are separate items in Note 18; they are not summed here because the sources describe the prepayments as written off together with a $25 million reimbursement.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected | Remediation |
| Principal holders and beneficial ownership are in the 2026 proxy statement, which is not supplied | Medium | Ownership and sponsor alignment | Supply the proxy statement |

| Executed debt and security documents (TrueBlue indenture and term loan, aircraft financing, Citibank agreement) are not supplied | High | Legal capacity, covenant and collateral analysis | Supply the agreements |
| Use of proceeds and lender identity for the April 14, 2026 financing are not stated | Medium | Transaction summary | Supply the related 8-K or agreement |
| Revenue benefit from Blue Sky, BlueFirst and loyalty initiatives is management-stated and not quantified in the filings | Medium | Revenue durability | Obtain management bridge if one exists |
| Unencumbered asset claim of approximately $7 billion not reconciled | Medium | Collateral, secondary liquidity | Obtain appraisal basis and encumbrance schedule |
| Events from October 27, 2026 to 2026-11-05 not supplied | Medium | Subsequent events | Supply later filings or confirm none |
| No debt maturity schedule by instrument beyond the aggregate table, no covenant certificate, no add-back bridge | Medium | Monitoring | Supply with the agreements |
## Next module

CP-2 (credit analysis) follows, then CP-5. CP-2 should use CP-1 metrics and this handoff's collateral, labor, fuel and financing facts, and should keep the unreconciled unencumbered asset claim out of its base case.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| JetBlue is a weak, liquidity-dependent credit: earnings do not cover debt service, but USD 2,226 million of liquidity and modest maturities through 2027 give time. Fare recapture of fuel costs decides the outcome. | Medium | Covenant levels, debt agreements and ratings are not supplied, so headroom and legal terms cannot be tested. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Computed EBITDA excluding special items for the last twelve months is USD 149 million against cash interest of USD 493 million, a cover of 0.30x. | Operating earnings do not fund interest; debt service depends on liquidity and new secured borrowing. | High |
| Net debt rose from USD 6,021 million to USD 6,767 million between December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026. | Liquidity is being consumed while debt is not being reduced. | High |

| About 88% of debt is secured and 66% of owned property, equipment and intangibles is pledged or committed. | Further secured borrowing leaves less unencumbered collateral for later needs. | Medium |
| Maturities are USD 629 million through 2027, then USD 1,835 million in 2029. | Near-term refinancing is manageable; 2029 is the pressure point. | Medium |
### Credit view

JetBlue Airways Corporation is a weak but currently funded credit: operating earnings do not cover its debt service, so it is living on its balance sheet. The strongest support is USD 2,226 million of liquidity at September 30, 2026, which includes a USD 600 million undrawn revolver to October 2029, together with only USD 629 million of debt maturing through 2027 and continued access to aircraft-secured funding. The weakest point is earnings: computed last-twelve-months EBITDA excluding special items of USD 149 million covers cash interest of USD 493 million only 0.30x, and free cash flow was an outflow of USD 1,193 million. What decides the outcome is whether fares keep recapturing unhedged fuel cost through 2027, and whether unencumbered collateral remains available as cash falls.
### Key findings

First, the earnings base is thin relative to the debt load. Computed EBITDA excluding special items was USD 350 million in FY2025 and USD 149 million for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, against debt of USD 8,393 million, which gives 56.33x gross and 45.42x net leverage [CP-1]. The issuer reports no EBITDA, so the ratios are our definition and are very sensitive to a small denominator; the direction is not in doubt, because the operating loss widened from USD 268 million to USD 509 million between the nine months of 2025 and 2026 [CP-1; Q3 10-Q page:6].

Second, the cash burn is funded by the liquidity cushion rather than by operations. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 273 million and free cash flow an outflow of USD 897 million in the nine months of 2026, while unrestricted cash and investments fell by USD 851 million to USD 1,626 million and net debt rose from USD 6,021 million to USD 6,767 million [CP-1]. The USD 495 million of new secured borrowing in 2026 offset only part of the USD 658 million of principal repaid.

Third, the structure is predominantly secured. Secured instruments are USD 7,455 million of the USD 8,450 million gross debt and finance lease obligations, and unsecured instruments are USD 995 million (Q3 10-Q page:11; calculation below). Of the secured amount, USD 2,733 million is the TrueBlue notes and term loan, secured by a first lien on loyalty program collateral and co-issued with JetBlue Loyalty, LP (10-K page:129, page:130). The 10-Q states that "Approximately 66% of our owned property and equipment and intangible assets at net book value were pledged or committed to be pledged as security under various loan agreements" (Q3 10-Q page:47). Mechanic: each new secured borrowing moves unencumbered value to secured lenders ahead of the USD 995 million of unsecured claims and any future unsecured lender; management's claim of about USD 7 billion of unencumbered assets is attributed and not reconciled (Q3 release page:2).

Fourth, the maturity profile is back-ended. Debt maturing is USD 152 million for the remainder of 2026, USD 477 million in 2027, USD 582 million in 2028, USD 1,835 million in 2029, USD 656 million in 2030 and USD 4,691 million thereafter (Q3 10-Q page:11). The 2029 amount includes the maturity of the USD 460 million 2.50% convertible senior notes and of the TrueBlue term loan facility, and coincides with the October 21, 2029 revolver expiry. Liquidity covers the fixed claims through 2027 (see Calculations) provided the revolver remains available and its minimum liquidity covenant is met.

Fifth, covenant headroom cannot be measured. Management states "we were in compliance with the material covenants of our debt and lease agreements" (Q3 10-Q page:47), but no level, step-down or reported ratio is printed for the TrueBlue financings or the Citibank revolver. The revolver "includes covenants that require us to maintain certain minimum balances in unrestricted cash, cash equivalents, and unused commitments available under revolving credit facilities" (10-K page:94). With unrestricted cash and investments falling, this is the test most likely to bind first; its level is Insufficient Information.

Sixth, operating exposures are unhedged and open-ended. The issuer had no fuel hedging contracts at September 30, 2026, and a 10% fuel price increase would add approximately USD 376 million of expense over twelve months (Q3 10-Q page:53). The pilot contract has been amendable since February 2025 and the inflight contract becomes amendable on December 13, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:19, page:20), so labor cost can step up without a revenue offset. Management says it recaptured approximately 87% of higher third-quarter fuel cost through fares (Q3 release page:1, Management Language); that recapture is the central assumption in any recovery of coverage.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Liquidity: USD 1,626 million of unrestricted cash, cash equivalents and investment securities plus the USD 600 million undrawn Citibank revolver gives USD 2,226 million, with no facility used in that figure expiring within twelve months [CP-1; Q3 10-Q page:14]. Documentary Fact. Funding access: the issuer borrowed USD 500 million against owned aircraft in 2026 and expects a further USD 250 million in the fourth quarter of 2026, which shows secured market access for aircraft collateral (Q3 10-Q page:13, page:14). Documentary Fact; the further amount is forward-looking. Governance: no sponsor or controlling holder is identified, no dividends are paid and no repurchase program exists [CP-1A; 10-K page:80], so no sponsor extraction channel is documented. Documentary Fact; beneficial ownership is Insufficient Information. Revenue momentum: Q3 2026 revenue of USD 2,812 million rose from USD 2,322 million in Q3 2025 [CP-1], with management attributing the growth to higher yields. Documentary Fact for the figures; Management Language for the attribution.

Weaknesses. Earnings and coverage: the 0.30x cash interest cover and negative free cash flow above are the core weakness. Documentary Fact for the inputs; Analyst Interpretation for the credit reading. Rising net debt and a thinning equity base: stockholders' equity fell from USD 2,120 million to USD 1,337 million and retained earnings turned to a deficit of USD 106 million between December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:6). Documentary Fact. Encumbrance: about 88% of debt is secured and a large majority of fixed assets are pledged or committed to be pledged. Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation. Concentration and operating shocks: 95% of routes touch six focus cities in a congested Northeast corridor, and disruption plus engine groundings (two aircraft grounded at September 30, 2026) reduce completed capacity [CP-1A]. Documentary Fact. Contingencies: the Northeast Alliance antitrust class action cannot be estimated (Q3 10-Q page:21) and the American Airlines contract claim carries an accrual of unstated size (Q3 10-Q page:22). Documentary Fact; loss is Insufficient Information.
### Credit assessment
| Dimension | Assessment | Category | Basis |
| Overall fundamental view | Weak, liquidity-dependent; confidence Medium | Analyst Interpretation | Earnings and coverage [CP-1]; liquidity and maturities [CP-1; Q3 10-Q page:11, page:44] |
| Business risk | Elevated: unhedged fuel, open labor contracts, Northeast concentration, single segment | Analyst Interpretation | [CP-1A]; Q3 10-Q page:53 |
| Financial risk | High: leverage in the tens of times computed EBITDA, negative free cash flow | Analyst Interpretation | [CP-1] |
| Liquidity | Adequate for the next twelve months on management's statement, declining | Documentary Fact (management statement) with Analyst Interpretation of the trend | Q3 10-Q page:44; [CP-1] |
| Structure | Predominantly secured; unsecured claims small and rank behind a growing secured pool | Documentary Fact with Analyst Interpretation | Q3 10-Q page:11, page:47 |
| Sponsor and governance | No sponsor extraction identified | Documentary Fact; ownership Insufficient Information | [CP-1A] |
### Capital structure and claims
| Instrument | Issuer or co-issuer | Amount (US$m) | Rate | Maturity | Security and guarantors |

| TrueBlue senior secured notes | JetBlue and JetBlue Loyalty, LP (co-issuers) | 1,991 | 9.875% coupon | September 2031 | First lien on loyalty program collateral, pari passu with the term loan; fully and unconditionally guaranteed by the Guarantors (identities in the indenture, not supplied) [10-K page:129, page:130] |

| TrueBlue term loan facility | JetBlue and JetBlue Loyalty, LP (co-borrowers) | 742 | SOFR plus 4.75% (First Amendment, February 28, 2025) | 2029 | Same collateral, guaranteed by the Guarantors; quarterly amortization; mandatory prepayment on collateral dispositions or change of control [10-K page:94, page:130, page:131] |

| Enhanced equipment notes, 2019-1 and 2020-1 series (five series) | The Company, through unconsolidated pass-through trusts | 1,055 | 2.8% to 8.1% at December 31, 2025 | Through 2027 to 2032 | Secured by aircraft [Q3 10-Q page:11; 10-K page:126] |

The five enhanced equipment note series sum to 409 + 128 + 38 + 407 + 73 = 1,055. Total gross debt and finance lease obligations are 8,450 and carrying value 8,393 (Q3 10-Q page:11, page:12). Guarantor identities and the issuer of each aircraft note are not named in the supplied text beyond "the Company".
### Claims outside the debt figure
| Claim | Amount (US$m) | Inside or outside the debt figure | Locator |
| Operating lease liabilities | 953 | Outside | Q3 10-Q page:6; undiscounted obligations 1,499 on page:46 |
| Flight equipment purchase commitments | 5,372 | Outside | Q3 10-Q page:17 |
| Other non-cancelable obligations | 1,673 | Outside | Q3 10-Q page:46 |

| Facility or test | Level | Reported or computed | Headroom | Note |
