Covenant requires minimum unrestricted cash, equivalents and unused commitments; level Not supplied. The July 29, 2024 amendment adjusted "the margin and the minimum liquidity requirements" (10-K page:137) |

| TrueBlue notes and term loan covenants | Debt service coverage ratios and minimum liquidity requirements; level Not supplied | Compliance statement only | Not calculable | Cross-default to other material indebtedness (Q3 10-Q page:47). Definitions differ from the EBITDA computed in CP-1 and are not known |
| Ratings | Not supplied | Not supplied | not applicable | Context ratings field is blank |

Liquidity of USD 2,226 million agrees with management's stated USD 2.2 billion (Q3 10-Q page:44). The issuer states liquidity is sufficient for at least twelve months from the report date; this is Management Language.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Earnings and coverage shortfall | Unhedged fuel and wage costs outrun fare recapture, keeping EBITDA below cash interest | Debt service relies on liquidity and new borrowing; default risk rises if recapture fails | Critical |

| Liquidity burn and covenant tripwire | Free cash outflow reduces unrestricted cash toward the revolver minimum liquidity covenant, whose level is unknown | Loss of revolver access would cut liquidity by USD 600 million | Critical |

| Collateral depletion | New secured borrowing consumes unencumbered assets; pledged assets are 66% of the base | Less room for later financing; more claims rank ahead of unsecured creditors | Material |

| 2029 refinancing concentration | USD 1,835 million of maturities, the convertible notes, the term loan and the revolver expiry cluster in 2029 | Refinancing at the same time needs earnings recovery by then | Material |
| Labor cost step-ups | Open pilot, inflight and new dispatcher contracts | Margin pressure; strike or slowdown risk | Material |
| Litigation | Northeast Alliance class action loss not estimable | Contingent cash call outside the debt figure | Material |
| Engine availability and delivery timing | Groundings and delivery delays cut capacity and shift capex | Revenue loss; capex timing uncertainty | Minor |
### Subsequent events up to the cutoff

LaGuardia slots purchase for an aggregate USD 58.5 million completed in October 2026, opposition to class certification filed October 9, 2026, and the expected fourth-quarter 2026 funding of USD 250 million of additional aircraft-secured financing (Q3 10-Q page:44, page:21, page:14). Nothing dated after October 26, 2026 is supplied.
### Conflicts and unreconciled items

- Payroll support loan rates: the 10-K rate table shows 2.0% for all three loans at December 31, 2025 and 2024 (10-K page:127), while the loan descriptions give 1.00% until April 23, 2025, January 15, 2026 and May 6, 2026 respectively and SOFR plus 2.00% thereafter (10-K page:131, page:132). The sources do not reconcile this, and the amount is small (535); this handoff does not choose between them. The rate column in CP-1 reproduces the table.
- Unencumbered assets: the management claim of about USD 7 billion is not reconciled to the pledged percentage (see Key findings).
## Calculations
All amounts US$ millions unless stated. Inputs are cited above or in CP-1.

- Secured gross debt at September 30, 2026: 43 + 409 + 128 + 38 + 407 + 73 + 573 + 619 + 2,011 + 1,991 + 742 + 421 = 7,455. Unsecured: 259 + 144 + 132 + 460 = 995. Total 7,455 + 995 = 8,450, equal to the gross total. Secured share 7,455 / 8,450 = 88.22 percent; unsecured share 11.78 percent (Q3 10-Q page:11).
- TrueBlue: 1,991 + 742 = 2,733, which is 32.34 percent of 8,450.
- Payroll support loans: 259 + 144 + 132 = 535.
- Maturities through 2027: 152 + 477 = 629. Unrestricted cash and investments cover this 1,626 / 629 = 2.59x; total liquidity 2,226 / 629 = 3.54x.

- Committed flight equipment spending for the remainder of 2026 and 2027: 185 + 385 = 570 (Q3 10-Q page:17). Maturities plus committed spending: 629 + 570 = 1,199. Liquidity 2,226 / 1,199 = 1.86x; unrestricted cash 1,626 / 1,199 = 1.36x. This is an illustrative comparison of fixed claims to liquidity before any operating cash flow, not a forecast.
- Last-twelve-months free cash outflow 1,193 against unrestricted cash and investments 1,626: 1,193 / 1,626 = 73.37 percent [CP-1].
- Change in stockholders' equity: 1,337 - 2,120 = (783) (Q3 10-Q page:6).
- Maturity shares of 8,393: 2029 1,835 / 8,393 = 21.86 percent; thereafter 4,691 / 8,393 = 55.89 percent; 2030 and thereafter (656 + 4,691) / 8,393 = 63.71 percent.

- Interest sensitivity: fixed rate 6.3 billion plus floating rate 2.1 billion = 8.4 billion, consistent with 8,393; a 100 basis point rise would add approximately 21 of annual interest expense (Q3 10-Q page:53). FY2026 interest expense guidance of approximately 590 less nine months 2026 interest expense of 440 implies approximately 150 for Q4 2026 (Q3 release page:3; Q3 10-Q page:6), a derived figure from approximate guidance.
- Leverage, coverage, free cash flow and net debt figures are CP-1's and are not recomputed here; a recheck of the LTM ratios gives 8,393 / 149 = 56.33, 6,767 / 149 = 45.42 and 149 / 493 = 0.30.
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters and what it affects | Severity | Action |

| Covenant levels and reported ratios for the Citibank revolver and TrueBlue financings not printed | Headroom drives the liquidity and default view | High | Supply credit agreements, indenture and compliance certificates |
| Executed agreements and Guarantor identities not supplied | Legal capacity and perimeter of security cannot be tested | High | Supply the agreements |
| Ratings and market data not supplied | No external check on the weak-credit reading | Medium | Supply ratings and quotes if a market view is wanted |
| Beneficial ownership not supplied | Sponsor alignment relies on absence of evidence | Medium | Supply the 2026 proxy statement |
| Loss estimate for the Northeast Alliance class action and size of the American Airlines accrual not supplied | Contingent cash outflow outside debt | Medium | Monitor docket and later filings |
| Management's fare-recapture and BlueFirst benefits not quantified in filings | The central recovery assumption is unverified | Medium | Request the management bridge |
| Events from October 27, 2026 to 2026-11-05 not supplied | Recent financing or litigation steps may be missing | Medium | Supply later filings or confirm none |

| Inherited from upstream: text extraction only; computed EBITDA definition; two debt totals on different bases | Figures depend on our definitions and on tables flattened in extraction | Low | Spot-check against the filed HTML |
## Next module
CP-5 (verification) follows. It should check the secured and unsecured split, the liquidity and maturity comparisons and the quoted covenant language against the filings.
